hints: Because numerator and denominator have equal degree, include a constant polynomial term in the decomposition.
Set the expression to $A+B/(2x-1)+C/(x-3)$, clear denominators, and determine all constants by substitution or coefficient comparison.
walkthrough:
Since the degree of the numerator equals the degree of the denominator, divide to find the constant quotient:
$$4x^2 - 13x + 13 = 2(2x^2 - 7x + 3) + R(x)$$
$$4x^2 - 13x + 13 = (4x^2 - 14x + 6) + (x + 7)$$
So the quotient is $2$ and the remainder is $x + 7$:
$$\dfrac{4x^2 - 13x + 13}{(2x - 1)(x - 3)} = 2 + \dfrac{x + 7}{(2x - 1)(x - 3)}$$

Set up partial fractions for the remainder term:
$$\dfrac{x + 7}{(2x - 1)(x - 3)} = \dfrac{A}{2x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x - 3}$$

Multiply both sides by $(2x - 1)(x - 3)$:
$$x + 7 = A(x - 3) + B(2x - 1)$$

Substitute $x = 3$ to find $B$:
$$3 + 7 = A(0) + B(2(3) - 1)$$
$$10 = 5B \implies B = 2$$

Substitute $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ to find $A$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2} + 7 = A\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - 3\right) + B(0)$$
$$\dfrac{15}{2} = A\left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right) \implies A = -3$$

Combine the quotient and partial fractions:
$$2 - \dfrac{3}{2x - 1} + \dfrac{2}{x - 3}$$

ai_rubric.Partial Fractions: Identifies the form $A+\frac{B}{2x-1}+\frac{C}{x-3}$; Derives one of $A=2$, $B=-3$, $C=2$; Concludes with $2-\frac3{2x-1}+\frac2{x-3}$.
